reviewContext.userProblem: nodetto has no way to draw electrical schematics. Users and AI agents need a `schematic` page kind, like the breadboard and PCB modes, where they can place schematic symbols, connect pins with orthogonal wires and explicit junctions, name nets with labels and get connectivity and electrical rule checks. The desktop editor, SVG/PNG export, the Bun CLI and the native CLI must be able to create, edit, lint, export and capture these pages, and the pages must interoperate with breadboard/PCB parity and KiCad import.
requiredOutcomes: A document with a schematic page can be created, edited, saved, reloaded and rendered in the desktop editor, the SVG export and the CLI capture, in both themes.
Connectivity and the electrical rule checks are covered by unit tests, including the junction and crossing rules and same-named net labels.
The native CLI (embedded interpreter) and the Bun CLI give the same lint and export results for schematic pages (native parity test, plan schematic-44).
Existing documents and all existing tests are unaffected; mise run verify and mise run test-cli pass; bun run typecheck passes under noUncheckedIndexedAccess-compatible typing.
docs/schematic.md describes the mode, the element types, the rules checked and the CLI usage; README mentions it.

Final integration gate, serial, after all plans land: bun run typecheck; bun run lint; CARGO_TERM_QUIET=true mise run verify; CARGO_TERM_QUIET=true mise run test-cli; CARGO_TERM_QUIET=true CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PWD/target/schematic-native-parity" cargo build --release -p nodetto-cli then NODETTO_CLI_TEST_BINARY="$PWD/target/schematic-native-parity/release/nodetto-cli" bun test apps/cli/src/native-parity.
nonGoals: Multi-sheet or hierarchical schematics, buses, global versus local label scopes.
Rubber-banding wires when a symbol moves; net highlight overlay and canvas-to-panel cross-probing.
Simulation, SPICE export, BOM export and footprint assignment for schematic pages.
User-defined symbol libraries (the IC box with an editable pin table is the escape hatch).
Writing .kicad_sch, back-annotation, or changing the desktop KiCad open flow (KiCad files keep opening as breadboard imports).
Native (Rust) awareness of schematic types; no Rust source changes.
No SCHEMA_VERSION bump, no change to existing page kinds, element types, file formats or other modes' tests.
No server, auth, secrets or deployment code; no push, no history rewrite.
constraints: Additive only: SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1; existing documents load and render unchanged.
packages/io never imports @nodetto/core; packages/core/src/pcb imports only itself; no DOM or Node APIs in packages/ir, packages/core or packages/io.
No new dependencies; bun.lock unchanged. English only, no emojis. Cargo runs with CARGO_TERM_QUIET=true.
Symbols, fixtures, rule texts and names are nodetto's own; nothing copied from KiCad, Fritzing or any other project; no names or data from user screenshots or issues.

Heavy per-pixel/per-vertex/per-byte work stays in Rust; per-element work linear; no regex-heavy or per-character loops in hot paths; new performance behaviour asserted with work counters, never wall-clock.
UI uses existing CSS tokens only, works in light and dark themes and is keyboard reachable.

Plans edit only their writePaths; files shared between plans are chained with dependsOn (overview 'Shared files and their single owner chain'); every successor on a chained file reruns the earlier owner's tests.

Per-plan gates are focused bun test runs plus bunx biome check on owned files; never bun run typecheck, bun run lint or mise run verify as a plan gate. At most two bun test or cargo processes at once across workers.

Workers follow the overview per-worker protocol: pre/post hashes, intent snapshots under tmp/schematic-s933/<planId>/, own progress log impl-plans/progress/<planId>.md, foreground commands with full logs, no git write operations, no repo-wide formatter.
Timing or deadline tests that fail in an aggregate gate but pass alone count as passing (record both logs, up to three attempts); existing tests and deadlines are never relaxed or deleted.
Never leave *.test.ts files under target/ or tmp/.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: One element type per symbol (18 schematic.* types: 13 parts plus power, wire, junction, label, noConnect); polarity variants are fields.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Breadboard precedent; per-type registry defaults keep types, edit add and validation simple (design 13 item 1).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Mirror reuses Visual.flipX; pitch 10 equals breadboard so snapBreadboardPoint is reused; rotation and mirror keep the anchor pin exactly fixed.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Reuse existing semantics and snapping without changing breadboard results (design 13 items 2-4).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Only pins, power pins, wire ends, junctions and label anchors join by coincidence; bends never do; a crossing without a junction is not a connection; the wire tool adds a junction only for a deliberate T.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Prevents polyline edits, labels or snaps from shorting crossing wires (design 13 item 5).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: One label namespace per page; labels join power nets of the same name.
ERC: unconnected pins, dangling wire ends and single-pin nets are warnings; duplicate references and shorted power nets are errors.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Breadboard precedent; drafts must lint (design 13 item 7).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Schematic as breadboard netlist source goes through the existing breadboard target card via mapKicadSymbol; invalid projections fail explicitly and leave the card untouched.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: No breadboard type, enum or rule change; equivalence test pins it to the KiCad netlist round trip (design 13 item 9).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: PCB parity is live against the first schematic page; PCB pages are linted only when a schematic page exists.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: PCB pages have no card and adding a pcb.* type is not additive-only; PCB-only documents unchanged (design 13 item 10).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: KiCad import onto a schematic page connects through net labels on pin stubs; KiCad files still open as breadboard imports on desktop; schematic import is the CLI schematic import.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: nodetto symbols have their own pin geometry (design 13 item 11).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Netlist text format is nodetto's own, versioned by its first line; the KiCad netlist reuses the existing writer through a widened structural input type.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Small, documented, reuses writer infrastructure (design 13 item 13, plan schematic-12).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Wires must be orthogonal (schematic.wireDiagonal); the row/column sweep lives in packages/ir/src/segment-sweep.ts shared by core and io.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Bounds all path lookups without a diagonal fallback; io cannot import core (design 13 items 15-16).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Electrical identity uses coordinateKey over roundCoordinate moved unchanged to packages/ir/src/keyOrder.ts; schematic coordinates limited to +-1e9; moves use canonical shared deltas.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Live and reloaded connectivity identical without changing JSONL output (design 13 item 18).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Existing KiCad importers are made linear without changing results, with brute-force oracle tests and work counters; diagonal lookups are counted and budgeted only on the schematic import path.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: The native interpreter must not inherit all-pairs scans (design 13 item 19, 14).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: UI wire draft reuses state.wirePoints and ctx.wireDraft; plan schematic-39 adds exactly one schematicWireNotice field to interaction.ts and interaction/types.ts; plan schematic-45 renders the notice with role=status.
Shared files are owned by single dependsOn chains and successors rerun predecessor tests.

Wire drawing and wire point editing share one target classification (plan 39 classifySchematicWireTarget); Shift comes from the pointer event (plan 39 owns one pointer.ts branch); start and finish junctions are committed with the wire in one batch; point edits keep untouched endpoints fixed with local orthogonal elbows, classify released ends like clicks, abort on a labelled crossing, and are keyboard operable through focusable handles (plan 46 edit logic, plan 45 handles).
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Design 7.3 revisions 9-10 and design 13 item 20 (revision 10 adds core exclusion before ranking in plan 47, classify-once commits, and resulting-index focus, comm-000050); review findings SCH-DESIGN-WIRE-SHIFT, SCH-DESIGN-WIRE-TWO-JUNCTIONS, SCH-DESIGN-DRAG-LABEL, SCH-DESIGN-DRAG-ANCHORS, SCH-DESIGN-HANDLE-KEYBOARD (comm-000048).
